//: The security boundary. Everything is deny-by-default; you grant surfaces here explicitly. Edit freely — it is re-read every heartbeat.

autoExecute.//: reversible: auto-run reversible allowlisted actions without asking. irreversibleAlwaysConfirm: queue every irreversible action for your confirmation even if it is allowlisted. dryRun: report what every call WOULD do and do neither — how to read a new schedule's task before letting it touch anything.

budgets.//: Call caps counted from the actions audit log. 'default' applies to any tool without its own entry; 'tools' overrides per tool. Absent or 0 = unlimited. Only executed/queued calls count — a denial cost nothing and shouldn't eat the allowance. Example: { "perRun": { "default": 8 }, "perDay": { "tools": { "web_search": 50 } } }

apps.//: Bundle IDs the mac_control tool may touch. Empty = the agent can control no apps. Find an id with: osascript -e 'id of app "Notes"'

userDirected.//: Irreversible actions that run WITHOUT confirmation when YOUR OWN chat message (typed or dictated) asked for exactly that action — 'email Jeff Houser that…', 'text Jeff Houser that…', 'add lunch with Sam Friday at noon to my calendar', 'remind me at 5 to…', 'make a note that…'. Entries are tool.action. send_mail and send_message additionally require the recipient to be someone you named in that sentence: an address or number the model found anywhere else (a web page, an incoming email) still queues for approval with the full message shown. Scheduled jobs, watchers, subagents and follow-ups like 'yes, send it' never qualify — they carry no request in your own words. Set enabled to false to confirm everything again.

trust.//: Tools whose irreversible calls run WITHOUT the confirmation queue, but only inside a live chat turn where you are typing. Schedules, watchers, the heartbeat and subagents still queue. Remove a name to put it back behind approval. Not listed on purpose: browser submit/buy/delete, and mac_control sends to anyone you did not name (those stay gated by userDirected).

web.//: Domains a future read-only web_fetch tool may read.

browser.//: Chrome control via CDP. enabled gates the whole tool. navigateAllowlist limits which domains it may open — [] means any domain. Risky clicks (buy/submit/send/delete) are queued for confirmation regardless.

google.//: Read-only Gmail + Calendar (gmail_search, calendar_upcoming). Requires a read-only token: npm run auth. The OAuth scopes are read-only by construction and must never be widened.

fs.//: Absolute directories read_file/list_dir may read from. Empty = no file access. e.g. ["~/notes", "~/Developer/agentspine/data"]. writableDirs is the (separate, narrower-by-default) list write_file may create text files in; absent or empty = it can write nothing. Overwriting or editing a file does NOT wait for approval — the old version is copied to backups/ first, which is why it is classified reversible. Two exceptions: a build manifest (package.json, Cargo.toml, build.rs, Package.swift, a lockfile, *.gradle) is queued for your approval because it decides what code the build fetches and runs, and AgentSpine's own policy.json, profile.md, goals.md and agents/*.md cannot be written by any tool at all.

weather.//: The weather tool (Open-Meteo, no API key). Gated not because the data is risky but because asking about your home town, on a schedule, tells a third party where you live. Set DEFAULT_LOCATION in .env so the location isn't restated in every run.

images.//: The generate_image tool: renders a PNG via the local MFLUX service (IMAGE_URL) and saves it under ./images, returning a URL the UI displays. Classified REVERSIBLE, not irreversible like a draft: it writes a new file into a directory it owns, overwrites nothing, and deletes cleanly — there is no outbound send and nothing to review before the fact, so queuing every render for confirmation would be friction, not safety. Enabling it here lets it auto-execute under autoExecute.reversible. The real cost it carries is compute: a render is 15-30s and the pipeline shares this 16GB box with capture and Whisper, which is a resource decision (bounded by MFLUX_MAX_SIDE on the service), not a security one. Disable by setting enabled to false.

drafts.//: SPEC §5, preferred path: the agent WRITES, you SEND. A draft is proposed text (email reply, new email, calendar event, note) that lands in the confirmation queue for review; approving it writes a file to dir. This grants NO new OAuth scope — the Google token stays read-only by construction and still cannot send or modify anything.

subagents.//: Delegation to the units in agents/*.md. A subagent's tools are the INTERSECTION of what its file declares and what its caller could already reach, so this grants no capability the agent did not already have — it only lets work be split up. Every call a unit makes still passes through this same broker and this same policy, and per-run budgets are counted across the whole tree rather than reset per unit.

schedules.//: Lets the agent read and change AgentSpine's OWN scheduler, so 'check for new movie trailers every day at noon' becomes a job on the Automations page instead of a thing done once. It grants a scheduled job nothing extra — a job runs through this same broker under this same policy. What it changes is when: a standing job acts while nobody is watching, and its task text is a prompt the model wrote, possibly influenced by something it read. So every create/update/delete is queued for your confirmation with the full task text shown, and nothing here can touch this file.

git.//: Absolute repo directories git_status may read. Read-only: branch, uncommitted files, recent commits. Empty = no repo access. e.g. ["~/Developer"]

build.//: The build loop. Each repo listed here is one the agent may work in: it can run the commands declared under it, and — with gitWrite — branch, stage, commit and diff. The model picks a repo and a command NAME; it can never supply a command line, and nothing it can call adds an entry here. Declaring a command is a statement that you trust THAT repo's build to run on this machine, since a test script and a build.rs are both code. allowPush is separate and absent by default; a push still waits for your approval even when allowed. parse names a reducer in src/tools/command-output.ts: cargo-json, eslint, tap, tsc, xcodebuild, or generic.

lint.description: web client only — src/ is not linted

build.description: compile for the iOS simulator (no signing)

audio.//: Microphone capture for meeting transcription. NOTE the inverted convention: devices is an allowlist and [] means NO device, not any device — an empty list is a safe default for reading web pages and an unsafe one for a microphone. List avfoundation input names exactly as `npm run listen devices` prints them. announce speaks a line out loud when capture starts, because the people being recorded cannot object to something they don't know about. macOS will also prompt for microphone permission the first time — a second enforcement layer the OS owns.
